rv.q: But the fragmentary structure, with few scenes stretching to any substantial length, paradoxically creates a sense of dramatic inertia that the vibrant performances cannot overcome.
Shifters may be a very small play but it strikes a symphony of resonant chords.
Shifters is a mosaic of meticulously cut and polished gems.

I felt the same about the couple in Shifters: this relationship ultimately tracks the failure of two people to be in the right place and time to be what and who the other needs, to heal each other’s traumas.
Ms. Lombe’s one-act play offers glimmers of insight, along with some platitudes, and Ms. Linton and her players deliver them with grace and charm.

The two smart and witty characters are playful combatants and reluctant soulmates; Heather Agyepong and Daniel Ezra portray them with convincing rapport and an engaging repertoire of precise and revealing gestures and expressions.

cn.t: Benedict Lombe's intimate two-hander earns praise for its universal meditation on love found and lost, elevated by the convincing chemistry and precise performances of Heather Agyepong and Daniel Ezra.
